title: Hatchery efficiency for turtle conservation in Cabo Verde
author: Martins, Ferreira-Veiga, et al.

steps.title: Select appropriate hatchery site
steps.instruction: Choose a location on the same beach, at sufficient elevation to avoid flood intrusion, and at a safe distance from plant roots; avoid sites that would require metal fencing.

steps.title: Construct hatchery fence
steps.instruction: Build a fence using wood and plastic materials (no metal mesh) with a bottom depth of 40–50 cm to keep out predators such as ghost crabs.

steps.title: Train all personnel
steps.instruction: Provide prior training for all staff or volunteers to standardize the relocation methodology and emphasize extreme care, hygiene, and avoidance of chemicals (e.g., mosquito repellent).

steps.title: Collect eggs from nests
steps.instruction: Carefully excavate in‑situ nests, counting each clutch, and keep eggs in their original vertical orientation; avoid vibrations and maintain high hygiene throughout handling.

steps.title: Transport eggs to hatchery
steps.instruction: Move clutches to the hatchery while avoiding sun exposure; if transport exceeds six hours, handle with extra care to preserve orientation and prevent damage.

steps.title: Place eggs at proper depth
steps.instruction: Deposit each counted clutch at the original nest depth or at the mean nest depth typical for the rookery.

steps.title: Fence individual clutches
steps.instruction: Enclose each placed clutch with plastic mesh to prevent hatchlings from escaping after emergence and to keep predators out.

steps.title: Guard hatchery if needed
steps.instruction: Maintain continuous guarding of the hatchery in areas where human exploitation is a risk.

steps.title: Record hatchling emergence
steps.instruction: Accurately count the number of hatchlings that emerge from each nest to determine emergence success.

steps.title: Exhume nests after emergence
steps.instruction: After hatchlings have emerged, excavate each nest and remove all eggshells and any unhatched eggs to assess hatching success.

steps.title: Manage nest temperature
steps.instruction: If the hatchery is too hot, provide shade or water the sand; if it is cooler than the beach, spread a 2–3 cm layer of black sand over each nest area immediately after relocation.
